questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: since I study european ethnology, I wanted to explore a culture with a rich history as well as an interesting social culture. above that it was crucial that the university had great options for subjects and classes. Edinburgh university had all of the above, and the city/country also seemed welcoming for international students, and a great environment for studying abroad. another thing was the climate, Scotland is not too different from Denmark, so I know it would feel more homelike, and I would really enjoy exploring.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: it was very difficult, there was so many things from Erasmus coordinators that was wrong, and a lot of wrong emails and so on. above that I didn't get accommodation, so I had to figure that out last minute. also the university is spread out around the city, and the system is different there. so not very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: no assisant.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: terrible, I ended up moving three times since the market is terrible in Edinburgh for finding acoomedation. and very expensive, I ended up being able to live in student accommodation for the last 2 months which was great, but I was about to have to go home from not being able to find accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: know the areas, and be certain your landlord isn't scamming you. I would recommend getting acomedation any time, it is way better than finding it yourself. and be in good time, dont rely on getting offered an acoomedation, so look for a place and have good contact with the people renting.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to find the courses I was interested in, then get them accepted at my home institution. after that I applied on Edinburgh universities website, were you register your classes and as an international student, were you put all your personal information as well as your record . I had gotten a confirmation mail from host uni were it said what needed to do to registrer. Then I could choose diffrent classes that I wanted, and I registered for a lot of them, and then I got a confirmation of which classes I was accepted to.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: you could contact the host institution, even though they were quite slow at answering, there was also a handbook that we got sent the last minute from the Erasmus coordintator in copenhagen.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: be certain of dates and deadlines, make sure you ask for help by writing emails to your host institution if you are uncertain. talk to other people that are going to exchange, and do it together.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the program was really great, impressive how the host institution included the students thoughts and ideas, and really made sure that the acedemedic program was up to date, and touched some current issues and there was a lot of student discussions.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the level of the courses was quite similar to home, but I seemed a but easier when I was there. to clarity, there was a lot of new students whom are around 18-19 years old, so the courses had a great structure and the teachers were very involved, and there were tutorials every week that you could go to and discuss the subjects. all in all the university of Edinburgh was 10 times more structured than copenhagen uni, and it was a lot more clear what the learning outcomes of the classes were, and what you should learn for each lesson. therefore it seemed easier, even though the material of the courses was about the same level as back home. but I will admit that because I didn't feel the same pressure as I do back home, the level of the courses felt less overwhelming and difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more structure, since covid was still active when I arrived, all of my lessons were prerecorded. and their website "learn" is the same as Copenhagens "abalon" but just a lot better. the teachers would use learn a lot more, and they were very clear on what had to be learned at so on. the students openions were taking a lot more into the teaching, and I was surprised at how they used what the students had to say a lot more. so all in all a great style of teaching, were they included the students more, made sure everyone understood what had to happen by making clear learning outcomes for each week. it made me realize how much copenhagen uni needs an update on abalone and their website, and they could definitely learn from Edinburgh university.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Object of desires 
Idenitty and experience in health 
social anthropology 1b

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i absolutly adored my identity and experience in health course. We were a lot of students from diffrent backgrounds, some very nursing students and others from anthropology. it was such a fresh course, that really dived in to current issues of health and the health system, with a fresh view. and the structure was so great, and really easy to figure out.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: that I had to pay 2 months of rent and I had one day, so be sure if you move that you have emergency cash. also the social events at the beginning of the year for exchange students really takes a toll on the wallet, if you want to be social and meet other people.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: the food was in general a bit cheaper, and nothing was really more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: there was a lot of clubs that seemed great, I was not a a part of any, but my friends seemed to enjoy them

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: diffrent clubs both athletic and cultural.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: go out on trips, and join the group chat of Erasmus exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: just make some friends, and hang out with them, don put too much pressure on having to see everything all the time, remember to enjoy the city and were you are. but I would recommend nature trips on the weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: okay easy, I got some great friends and we figured out the diffrent social things together.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: be yourself, go out a lot and just meet other peoples friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: hmm, not rellay any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: how sweet and open everyone is over there. so eye opening how we are and act in copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
prepare for housing and unexpected fees there. 
go to the library and study with your friends, and get outside. 
make sure to find some good friends the first 3 weeks and eat a lot of fish and chips.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: make sure to ask for help, study the map of where your classes are in the city, and just make sure to walk around a lot and get to know the area. and be prepared for unexpected things that will happen, and dont panic if they do, it will get sorted out

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: my amazing friends that I got there, I didn't know I could become so close to people in such a short amount of time. and seeing my own culture with new eyes, and bringing back som Scottish good energy and happiness to people of copenhagen.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: housing. absolutely terrible to figure out, but that is part of the adventure.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: be social, have fun and dont care about what others think, find a good spot in the city that you like, and visit that when you can.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
